text:
anya: Quick design review — rollback 'panic' affordance on mobile + keyboard. Problem: on narrow screens Panic is buried in the ••• overflow and keyboard users can't tab to it easily. Sketch attached (see thread) — want feedback on discoverability and accidental trigger risk.

matt: :eyes: saw this in usability lab yesterday. Mobile participants missed it every time.

jess: Agree it's hidden. For on-call flows we want near-instant access but also strong safeguards. Two needs conflict.

lex: Constraint: toolbar real estate on mobile is limited. Adding a persistent primary action will push other controls down. We can do a floating element but it affects map/list content.

sam: Proposal A: persistent mini "panic pill" docked bottom-left on mobile (small, high-contrast). Always visible, 1-tap opens modal with 2-step confirm.

sam: Proposal B: keep overflow but add a global keyboard shortcut + landing focus for desktop and an explicit accessible link top of page for screen readers.

jess: How about A/B testing both? Track accidental triggers, time-to-action, and SR users' path.

anya: UX concerns: visual weight (shouldn't panic users constantly), clear CTA color, and focus order for SR. Also copy — avoid alarming language in default state.

aria-bot: Accessibility checklist: add aria-label, role="button", focusable= true, visible focus indicator, announcement on open using aria-live, ensure 2-step confirmation has descriptive labels.

sam: Small CSS/ARIA example for the pill:
```
<button id="panic-pill" aria-label="Emergency rollback" class="panic-pill" aria-live="polite">Panic</button>
.panic-pill { position: fixed; left: 12px; bottom: 12px; background: #b00020; color: white; border-radius: 999px; padding: 8px 12px; }
```

sam: And keyboard shortcut suggestion (desktop):
```
// example with mousetrap
Mousetrap.bind('ctrl+shift+p', () => openPanicModal())
```

lex: Implementation notes: we can route the shortcut to a safe landing that requires confirmation. For mobile long-press we can detect touchstart + 700ms hold to avoid accidental taps.

lex: Example hold pattern (pseudo):
```
panicBtn.addEventListener('touchstart', startHold)
panicBtn.addEventListener('touchend', cancelHold)
// if hold >= 700ms -> show confirm modal
```

jess: Concern: keyboard shortcuts are discoverability problems for new users. Need a small tooltip/hint in the help menu and in the keyboard shortcuts modal. Also telemetry to know how often it's used.

anya: Proposal for next steps:
- Design: two micro-wires (persistent pill + overflow+shortcut) and a less alarming pill style copy.
- Research: 1-week prototype test (internal + a few beta customers) to gather accidental-trigger and speed metrics.
- Eng: build safe confirm flow + long-press + shortcut plumbing.
- A11y: run quick SR walkthrough and add aria-live announcements.

matt: +1 to prototype. For metrics, also track which method (pill vs shortcut vs overflow) led to action.

jess: I'll sync with PMs to pick beta customers and add to rollout checklist.

anya: I'll update Figma and push two micro-wires by EOD tom. If folks want to weigh in on copy I left three copy options in the figma comments.

lex: One more thought — add an optional org-level toggle (allow persistent panic pill) so enterprise customers can opt-in where space/flow permits.

anya: good call. Thanks everyone :+1:

sam: leaving a quick reminder to add keyboard focus order tests to the QA checklist.

aria-bot: Accessibility quick audit scheduled — report due in 3 days.

matt: we should put this on the design review agenda next Wed to go over the two micro-wires.

anya: noted, added to agenda.

jess: thanks all.
